question.text: Navratna Venture Fund (Cat I AIF) has three LPs: (i) Mr. Arjun Kapoor (resident individual, 40% units), (ii) Narayan Family Trust (resident, 35% units), (iii) Skyline Pension Fund BV (Netherlands-resident, 25% units). The fund distributes INR 20 crore of LTCG on unlisted shares (post-23-07-2024, non-business). What LTCG is allocated to the Dutch pension fund for its Indian tax return?

answer.text: Nil - non-resident LPs are exempt under Section 10(23FBA).
INR 20 crore - the full amount, because the fund is the legal seller.
INR 1.67 crore - split equally across the three LPs.
INR 5 crore - its 25% pro-rata share, retaining character as LTCG on unlisted shares.

explanation.text: The Logic: Pass-through preserves both the character and the proportion of income flowing through to each unitholder, mirroring what each would have earned had they invested directly. Skyline Pension's allocation = 25% x 20 crore = INR 5 crore, retaining character as LTCG on unlisted shares. The Trap: Option A wrongly exempts non-residents from the pass-through. Option B treats the fund as the taxable seller and ignores pass-through entirely. Option C splits equally rather than pro-rata to unit holding. Note: The workbook supports same-nature and same-proportion pass-through to unitholders, with non-resident investors generally covered in the same manner subject to Indian-source-income and treaty considerations.
